question: Queue item 20261030-1251-expand-dev-services-c696-u04-q01: what do the user-metadata limits of WorkOS, Clerk and Auth0 enforce? WorkOS: the documentation page (workos.com/docs/authkit/metadata) states up to 10 key-value pairs, while the OpenAPI specification (github.com/workos/openapi-spec) sets maxProperties 50 on the metadata of a user; both give keys of at most 40 characters and values of at most 600. Clerk: the page states metadata is limited to 8KB maximum without saying whether that is each of public, private and unsafe metadata or all three together. Auth0: the metadata limits page states a 10 KB user profile limit that is not yet a hard failure; a search snippet shows an Auth0 support article titled What is the Maximum Size of user_metadata and app_metadata Profiles with a figure of 16MB, but that article rendered through no reader route (a landing page or a loading shell), so only the limits page is quoted. Stytch states 20 top-level keys and 4KB per metadata object in three first-party places and needs no follow-up.
why: A write of 11 and then 51 metadata pairs on a WorkOS staging environment, a metadata write over 8KB on Clerk (one type, then all three together) and a profile write over 10 KB on Auth0 show what each service enforces. Each needs an account, so the step belongs to the operator.
